# Convolutional Neural Network

## Methods

### Question and task

-   Question: can a writer be identified from a single handwritten digit?

-   Input: one $28 \times 28$ image

-   Output: a probability for each of the 20 writers (softmax); the predicted writer has the highest probability

-   Each image is labelled with its writer, whatever digit it shows; the network is not told the digit

-   Split by session: train sessions 1 -- 3, validation session 4, test session 5

### Architecture and calibration

-   CNN: two convolutional layers (16 filters, $3 \times 3$), dropout, $2 \times 2$ max pooling, softmax output

-   Linear softmax: pixels straight to the 20 writers. Nearest centroid: average image per writer and digit

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
calibration <- data.frame(
  Hyperparameter = c("Hidden layers", "Activation", "Dropout rate", "Learning rate",
                     "L2 regularisation", "Epochs", "Told the digit"),
  `Default CNN` = c("2 conv.", "ReLU", "0.2", "$1 \\times 10^{-2}$", "none", "10", "no"),
  `Tuned CNN` = c("2 conv.", "tanh", "0.7", "$1 \\times 10^{-4}$", "0.1", "10", "no"),
  `Linear softmax` = c("none", "none", "none", "$1 \\times 10^{-4}$", "none", "20", "no"),
  `Nearest centroid` = c("none", "none", "none", "none", "none", "none", "yes"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

calibration |>
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    linesep = "",
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l")
  ) |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 8)
```

### Tuning

-   Stage 1: activation function, learning rate, dropout rate (72 combinations)

-   Stage 2: number of filters, kernel size, pool size (12 combinations)

-   Stage 3: number of epochs

-   Stage 4: L2 penalty $\nu$ (8 values)

-   Validation session only (session 4)

-   Average over three random seeds reported

### Metrics

#### Accuracy

-   Proportion of images assigned to the correct writer
$$\text{Accuracy} = \frac{\text{Correct predictions}}{\text{All images}}$$

#### Cross-entropy

-   Quality of the predicted probabilities (lower is better; guessing evenly gives 3.0)
$$\text{Cross-entropy} = -\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log \hat{p}_i$$

where $\hat{p}_i$ is the probability given to the true writer of image $i$

## Results

### Tuning the L2 penalty

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
nu_tab <- data.frame(
  nu = c("0", "0.003", "0.01", "0.03", "0.1", "0.3"),
  train = c(0.979, 0.979, 0.975, 0.957, 0.862, 0.165),
  val = c(0.591, 0.593, 0.600, 0.606, 0.612, 0.135),
  ce = c(1.892, 1.727, 1.529, 1.392, 1.447, 2.986)
)

nu_tab |>
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("r", "r", "r", "r"),
    col.names = c("$\\nu$", "Training", "Validation", "Cross-entropy")
  ) |>
  row_spec(4, background = "yellow!25") |>
  row_spec(5, background = "yellow!45") |>
  row_spec(6, background = "red!15")
```

-   Training and validation accuracy; cross-entropy on the validation session (mean of three seeds)

-   Dark yellow: value used ($\nu = 0.1$); light yellow: lowest cross-entropy; red: the model cannot learn

### Training versus validation

| Model       |  Training | Validation |       Gap |
|:------------|----------:|-----------:|----------:|
| Default CNN |     99.4% |      44.8% | 55 points |
| Tuned CNN   |     86.0% |      60.4% | 26 points |

-   The default CNN memorises the training sessions

-   Tuning halves the gap, but a large gap remains

-   The tuned score is optimistic: its settings were chosen on session 4

### Test performance (session 5)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
test_tab <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Nearest centroid", "Linear softmax", "Default CNN",
            "Tuned CNN (final)", "Guessing among 20 writers"),
  Accuracy = c("47.3%", "43.6%", "49.3%", "55.0%", "5.0%"),
  `Cross-entropy` = c("--", "--", "5.87", "1.39", "3.00"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

test_tab |>
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "r", "r")
  ) |>
  row_spec(4, bold = TRUE, background = "yellow!45")
```

-   95% interval for the tuned CNN: 42.7% to 67.1%

-   Versus the linear model: +11.4 points (95% interval 4.1 to 18.9)

-   Versus the default CNN: +5.7 points (interval $-1.9$ to 13.6), not distinguishable from zero

### Which writers, and where the errors go

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "100%"
recall    <- c(0.396, 0.576, 0.424, 0.404, 0.000, 0.840, 1.000, 0.764, 0.596, 0.292,
               0.676, 0.656, 0.004, 0.508, 0.796, 0.344, 0.852, 1.000, 0.600, 0.272)
precision <- c(0.343, 0.314, 0.731, 0.605, 0.000, 0.814, 0.628, 0.508, 0.603, 0.537,
               0.610, 0.594, 0.005, 0.599, 0.686, 0.637, 0.842, 1.000, 0.556, 0.249)
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
mids <- barplot(rbind(recall, precision), beside = TRUE, names.arg = rep("", 20),
                col = c("grey30", "grey75"), ylim = c(0, 1.25), yaxt = "n",
                xlab = "Writer (person_id)", ylab = "Proportion")
axis(1, at = colMeans(mids), labels = 1:20, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.8, line = -0.5)
axis(2, at = seq(0, 1, 0.2), las = 1)
abline(h = 0.05, lty = 2)
legend("top", c("Recall (accuracy)", "Precision"), fill = c("grey30", "grey75"),
       bty = "n", horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.8)
```

-   Writers 7 and 18: all correct. Writer 5: none. Writer 13: 1 of 250

-   Writer 10 $\rightarrow$ 2: 71% of images; writer 5 $\rightarrow$ 13: 60%

-   Writer 2 received 459 predictions, only 31% correct (fair share: 250)

### Conclusions and limits

-   A writer can be identified well above chance (55% against 5%), but not reliably

-   Likely reason: a writer's digits change between sessions by about 80% of the distance to another writer's

-   Limits: one validation and one test session, one training run per model, simulated data, a closed set of 20 writers




# Siamese Neural Network

## Methods

### General Siamese structure

-   Input: 2 or 3 images

-   Uses a CNN

-   Output: distance between embeddings of images

-   Distance infers dissimilarity

-   Contrastive loss:

$$L = yD^2 + (1-y)max(0, m-D)^2$$

#### Validation:

#### Test:

-   same writer, same session\
-   same writer, different sessions\
-   different writers, same session\
-   different writers, different sessions
-   sessions 1 - 5

### Metrics

#### Sensitivity

-   Proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified $$\text{Sensitivity} = \frac{\text{True Positives}}{\text{True Positives + False Negatives}}$$

#### Specificity

-   Proportion of actual negative cases correctly identified $$\text{Specificity} = \frac{\text{True Negatives}}{\text{True Negatives + False Positives}} $$

#### Balanced accuracy

-   Accounts for imbalanced classes $$\text{Balanced Accuracy} = \frac{\text{Sensitivity + Specificity}}{2}$$

### Default calibration

| Hyperparameter         | Value                |
|:-----------------------|:---------------------|
| Hidden layers          | 2                    |
| Activation functions   | ReLU                 |
| Number of filters      | 16 and $2 \times 16$ |
| Filter size            | $3 \times 3$         |
| Learning rate          | $1 \times 10^{-3}$   |
| Dropout rate           | 0.2                  |
| L2 regularisation      | $1 \times 10^{-3}$   |
| Layer 1 pooling window | $2 \times 2$         |
| Embedding length       | 16                   |
| Epochs                 | 15                   |

### Tuning

-   Hidden layers
-   Activation functions
-   Filter (square) size
-   Number of filters
-   Average validation performance metrics reported

## Results

### Tuning hidden layers

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
hidden_layer_tune <- data.frame(
  `Number of Hidden Layers` = c(1, 2),
  `Validation Loss` = c(0.214, 0.105),
  `Balanced Accuracy` = c(0.773, 0.966),
  check.names = FALSE
)

hidden_layer_tune |>
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("r", "r", "r")
  )
```

### Tuning activation functions


### Final model

#### Tuned inputs

-   Hidden layers: 2
-   Activation functions: reLU and tanh
-   Filter (square) size: $5 \times 5$
-   Number of filters: 16 and 32
-   Epochs: 6

#### Outputs

-   Test Balanced accuracy: 0.820
-   Test Loss: 0.104
-   Distance threshold: 0.247

### Session results

| Session Type |    n | Sensitivity | Specificity | Balanced Accuracy |
|:-------------|-----:|------------:|------------:|------------------:|
| Same         | 2000 |       0.899 |       0.995 |             0.947 |
| Different    | 2000 |       0.112 |       0.997 |             0.554 |
